# Pink Robotics: pinkrobotics.ca
> An engineering study of vacuum airships as a way to move large volumes of water to wildfires, based in Vancouver, Canada. Developed and maintained by the PinkAI infrastructure, directed by Tyler Dwyer. Some structural figures use a model with a Python-mirror parity gate; others are dated study assumptions or typed values. No aircraft has been built or flown, and no floating hull has been demonstrated.

Canonical pages:
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/ | the fundamentals and where to start
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/airships/ | the fleet monitor: a simulated fleet shown against wildfire, terrain and water data
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/airships/concept/ | how it works, one water cycle end to end
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/airships/engineering/ | the engineering, joint to ship
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/airships/ship/ | the ship, joint by joint, in 3D
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/energy/ | energy is cargo
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/research/ | the literature: 108 catalogue sources, including 10 marked as contradicting the project; nine selected objections are discussed on the page
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/animals/ | the animal partnership: a welfare-gated control architecture
- https://pinkrobotics.ca/log/ | the work log: what landed, who checked it and what it cost, generated from the repository

Pink Robotics belongs to Pink AI (https://pinkai.ca). The person: https://tylerdwyer.ca/about/. Contact: tyler@pinkai.ca. As of 2026-10-01.
